chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'This religion is robust, therefore delve into it with softness, and do not make the worship of Allah seem abhorrent to the servants of Allah, so you would become like the excessive rider who neither cuts (completes) a journey nor does a back (of an animal) remain (for him)'.
Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muqarrin, from Muhammad ibn Sowqat, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

key_terms.الْمُنْبَتِّ: The excessive rider / one who exhausts

ai.seo_question: How should one practice religion to avoid burnout and make worship appealing to others?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia principle of *taysir* (ease) in religious practice, warning against *ghuluw* (exaggeration) that alienates the common believer. The metaphor of the exhausted mount illustrates the practical necessity of sustainability in worship, ensuring that devotion remains a source of spiritual connection rather than a burden. This aligns with the Prophetic tradition of removing hardship, emphasizing that the religion is meant to be a manageable, enduring path for all people.
